correctness.rationale: Fischer–Freund necessary-and-sufficient dual contact-weight criterion for degree five has five real nonnegative inequalities. Writing h=c-a>0, Q(a)=2∏_{k=1}^5 T_k(a)>0, every contact numerator is a polynomial in h of degree ≤5 with zero constant. Independent SymPy reconstruction verifies 161 strictly positive nonexceptional coefficients (using rational bounds 2<sqrt5<9/4) and exceptional C_{2,1}(a)=(1-sqrt5)a^4 P(a²-1). P(v) has coefficient signs +----, P(1)<0<P(2), hence by Descartes a unique positive root v*=1.29023072795624.... For v<=v* all weights remain positive for every h>0; for v>v*, contact sigma_2 turns negative for all sufficiently small h. The endpoint is included; exterior c>a and complex polynomial coefficients handled by the published criterion. These are finite *exact identities* coupled to a valid general optimality criterion, not extrapolation from numeric r≈2.6492.

Their full primary text and contact criterion do not state the derived explicit quartic root nor an endpoint-inclusive iff global over all exterior real c. Resultary search returned only the submitted same-object exact-threshold finding; prior numerical coverage is acknowledged.

value.rationale: Degree five is the first degree for which the canonical normalized Chebyshev candidate can cease to minimize on an ellipse. The algebraic sharp shape threshold, an exact iff over continuum ellipses and all real exterior normalizations including equality, resolves a natural previously numerical boundary and furnishes a reusable test case for complex polynomial approximation.
